bugs.summary: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the item's key, but the audit-log endpoint orders by -datetime, so any non-empty page raises TypeError when the cursor is built.
bugs.evidence: paginator.py:840 `int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` with value = getattr(item, self.key); organization_auditlogs.py:80 passes order_by="-datetime" so BasePaginator.__init__ (paginator.py:63-65) sets key='datetime'; AuditLogEntry.datetime is models.DateTimeField (models/auditlogentry.py:69); build_cursor always calls key on results (utils/cursors.py:197 `prev_value = key(results[first_prev_index], for_prev=True) if results else 0`). Contrast DateTimePaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py:233-236), which converts via strftime first; value_from_cursor (paginator.py:842-843) likewise returns the raw int where build_queryset compares against the datetime column. Findings that flag value_from_cursor returning the raw cursor value for a datetime key (R2 v-sweep-high, 00-consensus-medium) are the same defect's second half (site :842-843) and match this entry.

bugs.summary: The endpoint dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access unconditionally, but member is None for requests without a member user (API key / org auth token), so every such non-superuser request to the audit-log endpoint raises AttributeError, even without optimized_pagination.
bugs.evidence: organization_auditlogs.py:71 `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` runs before the use_optimized check; RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is `RpcOrganizationMember | None` and documented 'member can be None when the given user_id does not have membership' (organizations/services/organization/model.py:344-346); the context is built from user_id=request.user.id (api/bases/organization.py:285-290), which is None for API-key/token auth (AnonymousUser, is_superuser False); OrganizationAuditPermission only checks scopes (api/bases/organization.py:110-124), so such requests reach line 71. R2 composite-high frames it as 'superusers without membership'; superusers short-circuit the `or`, but the non-superuser case it also implies is this bug.

bugs.summary: With enable_advanced_features and a client-supplied cursor with a negative offset, OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the Django queryset with a negative start, which Django rejects ('Negative indexing is not supported'), turning the request into a 500.
bugs.evidence: paginator.py:877-882 `if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0: start_offset = cursor.offset ... results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`; the cursor comes from the request and Cursor.from_string accepts any int offset (utils/cursors.py:53-61); Django QuerySet.__getitem__ raises on negative slice bounds. The endpoint passes enable_advanced_features=True (organization_auditlogs.py:82).

rejected.why: The class exists at head (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821); the import at organization_auditlogs.py:11 resolves.

rejected.was: BasePaginator.get_result passes unclamped negative offset when cursor.is_prev (paginator.py:182) (R2 22-medium, v-every-instance-*, v-no-speculation-low, v-grounding-medium)
rejected.why: Not introduced: base sliced queryset[offset:stop] with no clamping at all; the PR adds clamping for the non-prev case and leaves is_prev behaviour unchanged.

rejected.was: R2 00,01,12,21,22,composite-*,v-*: base paginator now silently clamps negative non-prev offsets to 0, returning the wrong window for all endpoints
rejected.why: Before the PR a negative offset reached queryset[offset:stop] and Django raised; clamping turns a 500 into the first page. Server-built cursors never carry negative offsets (utils/cursors.py build_cursor), so no valid request changes result.

rejected.was: R2 v-code-field-low/medium, composite-low, v-no-speculation-low/high, v-every-instance-low: trim check uses offset instead of start_offset
rejected.why: The trim branch runs only when cursor.is_prev, and on that path start_offset == offset in both BasePaginator (paginator.py:182) and OptimizedCursorPaginator (:877-882), so the check is equivalent.

rejected.was: R2 v-code-field-*, v-grounding-*, v-no-speculation-*, v-sweep-*, 22-medium: undocumented optimized_pagination query parameter / no feature flag / unrelated to stated goal
rejected.why: Design and process concern; the default path is unchanged and no behavioural defect follows from the switch itself.

rejected.was: R2 composite-medium, 22-medium: comment 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' is misleading (data beyond pagination bounds)
rejected.why: Comment only; the queryset is the organization-scoped audit log query the caller may already read, and negative slicing raises (b3) rather than returning extra data.

rejected.was: R2 12-medium, v-sweep-low: advanced path gated on a loose role check (superuser or has_global_access)
rejected.why: Intended: the same users already read the full audit log through the default path; the gate grants no new data.

rejected.was: R2 12-medium, v-sweep-low: cursors.py now accepts unbounded negative offsets / comment overstates
rejected.why: cursors.py change is comments only; Cursor.offset = int(offset) is unchanged from base.
